At the program/service provider level, this refers to individuals identified as being at elevated risk of HIV acquisition, including those requesting or receiving HIV prevention interventions, members of key populations, individuals with known risk factors, or those otherwise assessed as being at risk. At the population level, it involves estimating the size of each key population. HIV Incidence in PrEP Users: The rate of new HIV infections per 100 person-years (PY) of follow-up among PrEP users is calculated. This includes the number of individuals receiving PrEP who test positive for HIV during the reporting period and the total PY of PrEP use. Optionally, person-time contributed by individuals who do not retest for HIV or are lost to follow-up can be excluded from the denominator. 2. Adverse Events in PrEP Users: This includes the number of individuals experiencing adverse events while on PrEP during the reporting period and the total PY of PrEP use. Again, person-time contributed by those lost to follow-up can be excluded. 3. Sexually Transmitted Infections (STIs) in PrEP Users: The rate of STI cases per 100 PY of follow-up among PrEP users is assessed. This includes the number of PrEP recipients identified as STI cases through syndromic or etiologic approaches during the reporting period and the total PY of PrEP use. Person-time contributed by individuals lost to follow-up can also be excluded. 4. ARV Toxicity in PrEP Users: The percentage of PrEP users who discontinued or interrupted PrEP due to serious antiretroviral (ARV)-associated toxicity during the reporting period is calculated. This includes the number of individuals who discontinued PrEP due to toxicity and the total number of people on PrEP during the reporting period. This is based on survey responses to questions about drug injection in the past month and the use of sterile equipment. Opioid Agonist Maintenance Treatment (OAMT) The percentage of OAMT recipients who received take-away doses during the reporting period is calculated. This includes the number of individuals receiving take-away doses at least once and the total number of people receiving OAMT during the reporting period. HIV Testing 1. Time to Linkage to Prevention: This includes the sum of days from the test result to prevention uptake for all individuals testing negative and identified as being at elevated risk of HIV acquisition, excluding those already on PrEP. 2. HIV Testing Among Adolescent Girls and Young Women (AGYW): The percentage of AGYW seeking contraception or family planning services who received an HIV test is calculated. This includes the number of AGYW tested for HIV and the total number seeking contraception or family planning services. Treatment and Care 1. Co-Trimoxazole (CTX) Coverage: This includes the number of individuals living with HIV who started CTX and those newly enrolled in antiretroviral therapy (ART) and eligible for CTX. 2. Early Infant ART Initiation: The percentage of identified HIV-positive infants who initiated ART on the day of diagnosis is calculated. This includes the number of infants under 24 months of age who started ART on the same day as their HIV-positive diagnosis and the total number of HIV-positive infants identified during the reporting period. This includes the number of days between the test date and the date treatment was prescribed or dispensed. Cervical Cancer 1. Time to Treatment for Pre-Invasive Cervical Disease: The median time between diagnosis and treatment of pre-invasive cervical disease is calculated. This includes the number of days between the diagnosis date and the treatment date. 2. Loss to Follow-Up After Treatment: This includes the number of women who did not return for retesting 12 months after treatment and the total number of women treated 12 months ago. HPV Vaccination The HPV vaccine series for women living with HIV follows either a two-dose or three-dose schedule. HPV vaccination is included in the WHO ART treatment card and may be based on self-report or documented vaccine delivery.
